| Variable | Required | Description | 
|---|---|---|
| `keygen.Account` | Yes | Your Keygen account ID. You can find your account ID [here](https://app.keygen.sh/settings). | 
| `keygen.Product` | Yes | Your Keygen product ID. You can find your product [here](https://app.keygen.sh/products). | 
| `keygen.LicenseKey` | No | A license key used for API authentication. This will be used for license validations, activations, and for licensed upgrades. | 
| `keygen.Token` | No | A license token used for API authentication. This will be used for license validations, activations, and for licensed upgrades. | 

Whether to use `LicenseKey` or `Token` depends on the license policy's authentication strategy.
Setting it to `LICENSE` will require a license key, `TOKEN` a license token, and `MIXED`
will allow either. `LicenseKey` will take precedence over `Token` if both are provided.

If your product uses an `OPEN` distribution strategy, a `LicenseKey` or `Token` is not required.

#### Example main.go

`import "github.com/keygen-sh/keygen-go" func upgrade() error {  keygen.Account = "1fddcec8-8dd3-4d8d-9b16-215cac0f9b52"  keygen.Product = "1f086ec9-a943-46ea-9da4-e62c2180c2f4"  keygen.LicenseKey = "C1B6DE-39A6E3-DE1529-8559A0-4AF593-V3"   opts := keygen.UpgradeOptions{CurrentVersion: "1.0.0", Channel: "stable", PublicKey: "5ec69b78d4b5d4b624699cef5faf3347dc4b06bb807ed4a2c6740129f1db7159"}   // Check for an upgrade  release, err := keygen.Upgrade(opts)  switch {  case err == keygen.ErrUpgradeNotAvailable:    fmt.Println("No upgrade available, already at the latest version!")     return nil  case err != nil:    fmt.Println("Upgrade check failed!")     return err  }   // Install the upgrade  if err := release.Install(); err != nil {    panic("Upgrade install failed!")  }   fmt.Printf("Upgrade complete! Installed v%s. Please restart.\n", release.Version)}`

---

# Engines

Source: https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/

Engines are automatically populated by the current packages and their
releases. The below endpoints are read-only. To activate an engine,
create a package implementing the desired engine e.g. pypi, npm,
rubygems, etc.

An authentication token with privileges to read the release engine: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated engines.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with an engine object.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

An authentication token with privileges to read the engines: either an admin, the product the releases belong to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated engines.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with a list of engine objects.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Keygen implements the OCI distribution specification for container registries. The OCI specification is compatible with tools like Docker, Helm, and Skopeo.
For more information on the OCI specification, see opencontainers/distribution-spec. In addition,
we attempt to maintain compatibility with the Docker distribution specification, which can be found at distribution/distribution.
Keygen's OCI engine is an OCI-compliantpull-only registry.

You may also use the oci.pkg.keygen.sh subdomain, e.g. https://oci.pkg.keygen.sh/<account>.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Pull an image that implements the OCI engine using docker. Only packages that
implement the oci engine will be available for pull. Packages for other
engines, or packages without an engine, will not be available. In addition,
only packages which are available to the current requestor will be included,
e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN packages will be included.

Due to an upstream issue in the default
Docker Engine graphdriver storage engine (overlay2) i.r.t. how it handles authentication
in multi-tenant registries, you must use the containerd storage engine instead.
The default graphdriver engine does not respect registries that serve both unauthenticated
and authenticated requests, and is incompatible with Keygen's access control policies.
Instructions on enabling the containerd engine in Docker can be found here.
Docker Desktop has now transitioned
to containerd by default for new installs, and we expect the rest of the ecosystem
to follow.

For authentication, you have a couple options:

You can authenticate with a license key via docker login using --username license
and setting --password or --password-stdin to the license key value. The policy
must have an authentication strategy
of LICENSE or MIXED.

You can authenticate with an API token via --username token and setting
--password-stdin or --password to the token value. When using a license token,
the policy must have an authentication strategy
of TOKEN or MIXED.

Whether to use license keys vs tokens is a personal preference.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing images via docker push, and we
do not support other mutations such as deleting images or tags. Keygen's OCI
engine is a pull-only registry.

To upload a new version of an image, you can run docker build to build an OCI
image layout, and then use the Keygen CLI, the API, or the UI
to draft a new package release, then upload your image tar tarball.

The OCI engine ONLY supports images following the OCI image layout spec.
Uploading an image tarball that does not use an OCI image layout will fail
to be processed.

Similarly to Docker, you can use Oras to pull and inspect images. As with Docker,
please note that we DO NOT support pushing or deleting images or tags.
Rather, this can be performed via the Keygen CLI, UI, or API.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with the package metadata in JSON format.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the npm engine using npm. Only packages that
implement the npm engine will be available for install. Packages for other
engines, or packages without an engine, will not be available. In addition,
only packages which are available to the current requestor will be included,
e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN packages will be included.

For most use-cases, you'll be most successful using scoped packages, since it's
a lot easier to instruct npm to install all packages under @your-scope from a
private registry vs an unscoped package. In addition, we always recommend obtaining
the same scope on npm's public registry as well — otherwise a similarly named
package on the public npm registry may be installed instead of your package.

When installing packages via package.json, the easiest way to instruct npm to install
from your private registry is to use a package scope configured to point to a particular
registry — otherwise a similarly named package on the public npm registry may be
installed instead of your package.

You can instruct npm to install packages under a particular scope from a private
registry using an .npmrc file, or by configuring the registry via npm config.

Whether or not to use .npmrc vs npm config is a personal preference.

For authentication, you have a couple options:

You can set a license key using the :username and :_password parameters,
where :username is license and :_password is a base64-encoded license
key (note the value for :_password MUST be base64-encoded).

You can set an API token via the :_authToken= parameter.

Whether to use license keys vs tokens is a personal preference.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing npm packages via npm push.
To upload a new version of a package, you can run npm pack and then use
the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release, then
upload your tgz tarball artifact.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with a gem index in plaintext format.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the Rubygems engine using bundler or
gem. Only packages that implement the rubygems engine will be available
for install. Packages for other engines, or packages without an engine,
will not be available.

In addition, only packages which are available to the current requestor
will be included, e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN
packages will be included.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing Ruby gems via gem push.
To upload a new version of a gem, you can run gem build and then use
the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release, then
upload your gem artifacts.

When installing gems, the source method must be used to instruct Rubygems to install
from an alternative source. You may provide authentication in the source directly,
or you can define the credentials globally via .gemrc, which will let bundler
and gem install gems without having to hard-code authentication into the
source definition.

Keygen implements PyPI's simple repository format for pip packages. Artifact metadata will be visible as data-* attributes, e.g. requiresPython will become data-requires-python.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with an HTML document containing
links to the package artifacts, in accordance with PEP 503.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the pypi engine using pip. Only
packages that implement the pypi engine will be available for
install. Packages for other engines, or packages without an
engine, will not be available.

In addition, only packages which are available to the current requestor
will be included, e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN
packages will be included.

Please prefer --index-url over --extra-index-url, for security reasons.
Because pip does not lock dependencies to specific repositories, and because
pip provides no protection from package spoofing, we recommend using Keygen
as the sole package index. All non-Keygen packages will be securely
redirected to PyPI for fulfillment (also known as a "pass through"
PyPI repository).

This prevents pip from installing a package with the same name from PyPI
instead of Keygen, preventing a supply chain attack vector.

Alternatively, you can add the --index-url flag to your requirements.txt.

Alternatively, you can configure the engine globally via pypi.conf. This will
make pip install all packages through Keygen. Keygen is a pass-through
PyPI repository, meaning we will redirect all non-Keygen packages to PyPI.

Please see earlier security notice on --index-url vs --extra-index-url.

Alternatively, you can configure the engine globally via .pypirc.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support uploading Python packages via twine.
To upload a new version of a package, you can run python setup.py bdist_wheel sdist
and then use the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release,
then upload your whl and other distribution artifacts.

Keygen does not support Squirrel.Mac or Squirrel.Windows yet, but we have an official integration
with electron-builder that we recommend
instead. It is easier to integrate with across platforms, and more secure.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

The version constraint for the upgrade. For example, constraint=1.0 will constrain all upgrades to version 1.x, while constraint=1.0.0 will constrain to version 1.0.x. This is useful if a given license is only entitled to a specific version range. Major version is required.

You can also use constraints to constrain to a specific prerelease tag, such as constraint=1-beta, or to a specific build tag like constraint=1%2Bfoo (note the URL-encoded + symbol).

The release channel. One of: stable, rc, beta, alpha or dev. The rc channel will include stable releases. The beta channel will include rc and stable. Alpha will include beta, rc, and stable. Dev will only include releases on the dev channel (you can think of it as 'nightly' or 'edge', i.e. following a master branch).

A 200 OK response will be returned along with the update object.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

You can use Keygen with Tauri's native updater
to implement auto-updates for your Tauri app. Releases can be drafted
and artifacts uploaded via the CLI or UI.

Please note that signatures MUST be explicitly set on uploaded artifacts.
We do not automatically read accompanying .sig artifacts.

Using the CLI, this would look something like this:

The raw engine can be to create dynamic artifact download links that point to raw binaries, installers, etc.
These artifact download links are scoped to a product, package, and release. When the release does not have
a package, the package may be omitted.

You may also use the raw.pkg.keygen.sh subdomain, e.g. https://raw.pkg.keygen.sh/<account>/<product>[/@<package>]/<release>/<artifact>.

An authentication token with privileges to read the artifacts: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 303 See Other redirect will be returned, pointing to the artifact's canonical URL.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Whether to use license keys vs tokens is a personal preference.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing images via docker push, and we
do not support other mutations such as deleting images or tags. Keygen's OCI
engine is a pull-only registry.

To upload a new version of an image, you can run docker build to build an OCI
image layout, and then use the Keygen CLI, the API, or the UI
to draft a new package release, then upload your image tar tarball.

The OCI engine ONLY supports images following the OCI image layout spec.
Uploading an image tarball that does not use an OCI image layout will fail
to be processed.

Similarly to Docker, you can use Oras to pull and inspect images. As with Docker,
please note that we DO NOT support pushing or deleting images or tags.
Rather, this can be performed via the Keygen CLI, UI, or API.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with the package metadata in JSON format.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the npm engine using npm. Only packages that
implement the npm engine will be available for install. Packages for other
engines, or packages without an engine, will not be available. In addition,
only packages which are available to the current requestor will be included,
e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN packages will be included.

For most use-cases, you'll be most successful using scoped packages, since it's
a lot easier to instruct npm to install all packages under @your-scope from a
private registry vs an unscoped package. In addition, we always recommend obtaining
the same scope on npm's public registry as well — otherwise a similarly named
package on the public npm registry may be installed instead of your package.

When installing packages via package.json, the easiest way to instruct npm to install
from your private registry is to use a package scope configured to point to a particular
registry — otherwise a similarly named package on the public npm registry may be
installed instead of your package.

You can instruct npm to install packages under a particular scope from a private
registry using an .npmrc file, or by configuring the registry via npm config.

Whether or not to use .npmrc vs npm config is a personal preference.

For authentication, you have a couple options:

You can set a license key using the :username and :_password parameters,
where :username is license and :_password is a base64-encoded license
key (note the value for :_password MUST be base64-encoded).

You can set an API token via the :_authToken= parameter.

Whether to use license keys vs tokens is a personal preference.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing npm packages via npm push.
To upload a new version of a package, you can run npm pack and then use
the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release, then
upload your tgz tarball artifact.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with a gem index in plaintext format.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the Rubygems engine using bundler or
gem. Only packages that implement the rubygems engine will be available
for install. Packages for other engines, or packages without an engine,
will not be available.

In addition, only packages which are available to the current requestor
will be included, e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN
packages will be included.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing Ruby gems via gem push.
To upload a new version of a gem, you can run gem build and then use
the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release, then
upload your gem artifacts.

When installing gems, the source method must be used to instruct Rubygems to install
from an alternative source. You may provide authentication in the source directly,
or you can define the credentials globally via .gemrc, which will let bundler
and gem install gems without having to hard-code authentication into the
source definition.

Keygen implements PyPI's simple repository format for pip packages. Artifact metadata will be visible as data-* attributes, e.g. requiresPython will become data-requires-python.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with an HTML document containing
links to the package artifacts, in accordance with PEP 503.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the pypi engine using pip. Only
packages that implement the pypi engine will be available for
install. Packages for other engines, or packages without an
engine, will not be available.

In addition, only packages which are available to the current requestor
will be included, e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN
packages will be included.

Please prefer --index-url over --extra-index-url, for security reasons.
Because pip does not lock dependencies to specific repositories, and because
pip provides no protection from package spoofing, we recommend using Keygen
as the sole package index. All non-Keygen packages will be securely
redirected to PyPI for fulfillment (also known as a "pass through"
PyPI repository).

This prevents pip from installing a package with the same name from PyPI
instead of Keygen, preventing a supply chain attack vector.

Alternatively, you can add the --index-url flag to your requirements.txt.

Alternatively, you can configure the engine globally via pypi.conf. This will
make pip install all packages through Keygen. Keygen is a pass-through
PyPI repository, meaning we will redirect all non-Keygen packages to PyPI.

Please see earlier security notice on --index-url vs --extra-index-url.

Alternatively, you can configure the engine globally via .pypirc.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support uploading Python packages via twine.
To upload a new version of a package, you can run python setup.py bdist_wheel sdist
and then use the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release,
then upload your whl and other distribution artifacts.

Keygen does not support Squirrel.Mac or Squirrel.Windows yet, but we have an official integration
with electron-builder that we recommend
instead. It is easier to integrate with across platforms, and more secure.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

The version constraint for the upgrade. For example, constraint=1.0 will constrain all upgrades to version 1.x, while constraint=1.0.0 will constrain to version 1.0.x. This is useful if a given license is only entitled to a specific version range. Major version is required.

You can also use constraints to constrain to a specific prerelease tag, such as constraint=1-beta, or to a specific build tag like constraint=1%2Bfoo (note the URL-encoded + symbol).

The release channel. One of: stable, rc, beta, alpha or dev. The rc channel will include stable releases. The beta channel will include rc and stable. Alpha will include beta, rc, and stable. Dev will only include releases on the dev channel (you can think of it as 'nightly' or 'edge', i.e. following a master branch).

A 200 OK response will be returned along with the update object.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

You can use Keygen with Tauri's native updater
to implement auto-updates for your Tauri app. Releases can be drafted
and artifacts uploaded via the CLI or UI.

Please note that signatures MUST be explicitly set on uploaded artifacts.
We do not automatically read accompanying .sig artifacts.

Using the CLI, this would look something like this:

The raw engine can be to create dynamic artifact download links that point to raw binaries, installers, etc.
These artifact download links are scoped to a product, package, and release. When the release does not have
a package, the package may be omitted.

You may also use the raw.pkg.keygen.sh subdomain, e.g. https://raw.pkg.keygen.sh/<account>/<product>[/@<package>]/<release>/<artifact>.

An authentication token with privileges to read the artifacts: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 303 See Other redirect will be returned, pointing to the artifact's canonical URL.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

# List all engines

Source: https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-list

Engines are automatically populated by the current packages and their
releases. The below endpoints are read-only. To activate an engine,
create a package implementing the desired engine e.g. pypi, npm,
rubygems, etc.

An authentication token with privileges to read the release engine: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated engines.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with an engine object.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

An authentication token with privileges to read the engines: either an admin, the product the releases belong to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated engines.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with a list of engine objects.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Keygen implements the OCI distribution specification for container registries. The OCI specification is compatible with tools like Docker, Helm, and Skopeo.
For more information on the OCI specification, see opencontainers/distribution-spec. In addition,
we attempt to maintain compatibility with the Docker distribution specification, which can be found at distribution/distribution.
Keygen's OCI engine is an OCI-compliantpull-only registry.

You may also use the oci.pkg.keygen.sh subdomain, e.g. https://oci.pkg.keygen.sh/<account>.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Pull an image that implements the OCI engine using docker. Only packages that
implement the oci engine will be available for pull. Packages for other
engines, or packages without an engine, will not be available. In addition,
only packages which are available to the current requestor will be included,
e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN packages will be included.

Due to an upstream issue in the default
Docker Engine graphdriver storage engine (overlay2) i.r.t. how it handles authentication
in multi-tenant registries, you must use the containerd storage engine instead.
The default graphdriver engine does not respect registries that serve both unauthenticated
and authenticated requests, and is incompatible with Keygen's access control policies.
Instructions on enabling the containerd engine in Docker can be found here.
Docker Desktop has now transitioned
to containerd by default for new installs, and we expect the rest of the ecosystem
to follow.

For authentication, you have a couple options:

You can authenticate with a license key via docker login using --username license
and setting --password or --password-stdin to the license key value. The policy
must have an authentication strategy
of LICENSE or MIXED.

You can authenticate with an API token via --username token and setting
--password-stdin or --password to the token value. When using a license token,
the policy must have an authentication strategy
of TOKEN or MIXED.

Whether to use license keys vs tokens is a personal preference.

This prevents pip from installing a package with the same name from PyPI
instead of Keygen, preventing a supply chain attack vector.

Alternatively, you can add the --index-url flag to your requirements.txt.

Alternatively, you can configure the engine globally via pypi.conf. This will
make pip install all packages through Keygen. Keygen is a pass-through
PyPI repository, meaning we will redirect all non-Keygen packages to PyPI.

Please see earlier security notice on --index-url vs --extra-index-url.

Alternatively, you can configure the engine globally via .pypirc.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support uploading Python packages via twine.
To upload a new version of a package, you can run python setup.py bdist_wheel sdist
and then use the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release,
then upload your whl and other distribution artifacts.

Keygen does not support Squirrel.Mac or Squirrel.Windows yet, but we have an official integration
with electron-builder that we recommend
instead. It is easier to integrate with across platforms, and more secure.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

The version constraint for the upgrade. For example, constraint=1.0 will constrain all upgrades to version 1.x, while constraint=1.0.0 will constrain to version 1.0.x. This is useful if a given license is only entitled to a specific version range. Major version is required.

You can also use constraints to constrain to a specific prerelease tag, such as constraint=1-beta, or to a specific build tag like constraint=1%2Bfoo (note the URL-encoded + symbol).

The release channel. One of: stable, rc, beta, alpha or dev. The rc channel will include stable releases. The beta channel will include rc and stable. Alpha will include beta, rc, and stable. Dev will only include releases on the dev channel (you can think of it as 'nightly' or 'edge', i.e. following a master branch).

A 200 OK response will be returned along with the update object.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

You can use Keygen with Tauri's native updater
to implement auto-updates for your Tauri app. Releases can be drafted
and artifacts uploaded via the CLI or UI.

Please note that signatures MUST be explicitly set on uploaded artifacts.
We do not automatically read accompanying .sig artifacts.

Using the CLI, this would look something like this:

The raw engine can be to create dynamic artifact download links that point to raw binaries, installers, etc.
These artifact download links are scoped to a product, package, and release. When the release does not have
a package, the package may be omitted.

You may also use the raw.pkg.keygen.sh subdomain, e.g. https://raw.pkg.keygen.sh/<account>/<product>[/@<package>]/<release>/<artifact>.

An authentication token with privileges to read the artifacts: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 303 See Other redirect will be returned, pointing to the artifact's canonical URL.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

# npm engine

Source: https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-npm

Engines are automatically populated by the current packages and their
releases. The below endpoints are read-only. To activate an engine,
create a package implementing the desired engine e.g. pypi, npm,
rubygems, etc.

An authentication token with privileges to read the release engine: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated engines.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with an engine object.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

An authentication token with privileges to read the engines: either an admin, the product the releases belong to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated engines.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with a list of engine objects.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Keygen implements the OCI distribution specification for container registries. The OCI specification is compatible with tools like Docker, Helm, and Skopeo.
For more information on the OCI specification, see opencontainers/distribution-spec. In addition,
we attempt to maintain compatibility with the Docker distribution specification, which can be found at distribution/distribution.
Keygen's OCI engine is an OCI-compliantpull-only registry.

You may also use the oci.pkg.keygen.sh subdomain, e.g. https://oci.pkg.keygen.sh/<account>.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Pull an image that implements the OCI engine using docker. Only packages that
implement the oci engine will be available for pull. Packages for other
engines, or packages without an engine, will not be available. In addition,
only packages which are available to the current requestor will be included,
e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN packages will be included.

Due to an upstream issue in the default
Docker Engine graphdriver storage engine (overlay2) i.r.t. how it handles authentication
in multi-tenant registries, you must use the containerd storage engine instead.
The default graphdriver engine does not respect registries that serve both unauthenticated
and authenticated requests, and is incompatible with Keygen's access control policies.
Instructions on enabling the containerd engine in Docker can be found here.
Docker Desktop has now transitioned
to containerd by default for new installs, and we expect the rest of the ecosystem
to follow.

For authentication, you have a couple options:

You can authenticate with a license key via docker login using --username license
and setting --password or --password-stdin to the license key value. The policy
must have an authentication strategy
of LICENSE or MIXED.

You can authenticate with an API token via --username token and setting
--password-stdin or --password to the token value. When using a license token,
the policy must have an authentication strategy
of TOKEN or MIXED.

Whether to use license keys vs tokens is a personal preference.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing images via docker push, and we
do not support other mutations such as deleting images or tags. Keygen's OCI
engine is a pull-only registry.

To upload a new version of an image, you can run docker build to build an OCI
image layout, and then use the Keygen CLI, the API, or the UI
to draft a new package release, then upload your image tar tarball.

The OCI engine ONLY supports images following the OCI image layout spec.
Uploading an image tarball that does not use an OCI image layout will fail
to be processed.

Similarly to Docker, you can use Oras to pull and inspect images. As with Docker,
please note that we DO NOT support pushing or deleting images or tags.
Rather, this can be performed via the Keygen CLI, UI, or API.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with the package metadata in JSON format.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the npm engine using npm. Only packages that
implement the npm engine will be available for install. Packages for other
engines, or packages without an engine, will not be available. In addition,
only packages which are available to the current requestor will be included,
e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN packages will be included.

For most use-cases, you'll be most successful using scoped packages, since it's
a lot easier to instruct npm to install all packages under @your-scope from a
private registry vs an unscoped package. In addition, we always recommend obtaining
the same scope on npm's public registry as well — otherwise a similarly named
package on the public npm registry may be installed instead of your package.

When installing packages via package.json, the easiest way to instruct npm to install
from your private registry is to use a package scope configured to point to a particular
registry — otherwise a similarly named package on the public npm registry may be
installed instead of your package.

You can instruct npm to install packages under a particular scope from a private
registry using an .npmrc file, or by configuring the registry via npm config.

Whether or not to use .npmrc vs npm config is a personal preference.

For authentication, you have a couple options:

You can set a license key using the :username and :_password parameters,
where :username is license and :_password is a base64-encoded license
key (note the value for :_password MUST be base64-encoded).

You can set an API token via the :_authToken= parameter.

Whether to use license keys vs tokens is a personal preference.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing npm packages via npm push.
To upload a new version of a package, you can run npm pack and then use
the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release, then
upload your tgz tarball artifact.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with a gem index in plaintext format.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the Rubygems engine using bundler or
gem. Only packages that implement the rubygems engine will be available
for install. Packages for other engines, or packages without an engine,
will not be available.

In addition, only packages which are available to the current requestor
will be included, e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN
packages will be included.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing Ruby gems via gem push.
To upload a new version of a gem, you can run gem build and then use
the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release, then
upload your gem artifacts.

When installing gems, the source method must be used to instruct Rubygems to install
from an alternative source. You may provide authentication in the source directly,
or you can define the credentials globally via .gemrc, which will let bundler
and gem install gems without having to hard-code authentication into the
source definition.

Keygen implements PyPI's simple repository format for pip packages. Artifact metadata will be visible as data-* attributes, e.g. requiresPython will become data-requires-python.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with an HTML document containing
links to the package artifacts, in accordance with PEP 503.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the pypi engine using pip. Only
packages that implement the pypi engine will be available for
install. Packages for other engines, or packages without an
engine, will not be available.

In addition, only packages which are available to the current requestor
will be included, e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN
packages will be included.

Please prefer --index-url over --extra-index-url, for security reasons.

Please see earlier security notice on --index-url vs --extra-index-url.

engines, or packages without an engine, will not be available. In addition,
only packages which are available to the current requestor will be included,
e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN packages will be included.

Due to an upstream issue in the default
Docker Engine graphdriver storage engine (overlay2) i.r.t. how it handles authentication
in multi-tenant registries, you must use the containerd storage engine instead.
The default graphdriver engine does not respect registries that serve both unauthenticated
and authenticated requests, and is incompatible with Keygen's access control policies.
Instructions on enabling the containerd engine in Docker can be found here.
Docker Desktop has now transitioned
to containerd by default for new installs, and we expect the rest of the ecosystem
to follow.

For authentication, you have a couple options:

You can authenticate with a license key via docker login using --username license
and setting --password or --password-stdin to the license key value. The policy
must have an authentication strategy
of LICENSE or MIXED.

You can authenticate with an API token via --username token and setting
--password-stdin or --password to the token value. When using a license token,
the policy must have an authentication strategy
of TOKEN or MIXED.

Whether to use license keys vs tokens is a personal preference.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing images via docker push, and we
do not support other mutations such as deleting images or tags. Keygen's OCI
engine is a pull-only registry.

To upload a new version of an image, you can run docker build to build an OCI
image layout, and then use the Keygen CLI, the API, or the UI
to draft a new package release, then upload your image tar tarball.

The OCI engine ONLY supports images following the OCI image layout spec.
Uploading an image tarball that does not use an OCI image layout will fail
to be processed.

Similarly to Docker, you can use Oras to pull and inspect images. As with Docker,
please note that we DO NOT support pushing or deleting images or tags.
Rather, this can be performed via the Keygen CLI, UI, or API.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with the package metadata in JSON format.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the npm engine using npm. Only packages that
implement the npm engine will be available for install. Packages for other
engines, or packages without an engine, will not be available. In addition,
only packages which are available to the current requestor will be included,
e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN packages will be included.

For most use-cases, you'll be most successful using scoped packages, since it's
a lot easier to instruct npm to install all packages under @your-scope from a
private registry vs an unscoped package. In addition, we always recommend obtaining
the same scope on npm's public registry as well — otherwise a similarly named
package on the public npm registry may be installed instead of your package.

When installing packages via package.json, the easiest way to instruct npm to install
from your private registry is to use a package scope configured to point to a particular
registry — otherwise a similarly named package on the public npm registry may be
installed instead of your package.

You can instruct npm to install packages under a particular scope from a private
registry using an .npmrc file, or by configuring the registry via npm config.

Whether or not to use .npmrc vs npm config is a personal preference.

For authentication, you have a couple options:

You can set a license key using the :username and :_password parameters,
where :username is license and :_password is a base64-encoded license
key (note the value for :_password MUST be base64-encoded).

You can set an API token via the :_authToken= parameter.

Whether to use license keys vs tokens is a personal preference.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing npm packages via npm push.
To upload a new version of a package, you can run npm pack and then use
the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release, then
upload your tgz tarball artifact.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with a gem index in plaintext format.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the Rubygems engine using bundler or
gem. Only packages that implement the rubygems engine will be available
for install. Packages for other engines, or packages without an engine,
will not be available.

In addition, only packages which are available to the current requestor
will be included, e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN
packages will be included.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing Ruby gems via gem push.
To upload a new version of a gem, you can run gem build and then use
the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release, then
upload your gem artifacts.

When installing gems, the source method must be used to instruct Rubygems to install
from an alternative source. You may provide authentication in the source directly,
or you can define the credentials globally via .gemrc, which will let bundler
and gem install gems without having to hard-code authentication into the
source definition.

Keygen implements PyPI's simple repository format for pip packages. Artifact metadata will be visible as data-* attributes, e.g. requiresPython will become data-requires-python.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with an HTML document containing
links to the package artifacts, in accordance with PEP 503.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the pypi engine using pip. Only
packages that implement the pypi engine will be available for
install. Packages for other engines, or packages without an
engine, will not be available.

In addition, only packages which are available to the current requestor
will be included, e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN
packages will be included.

Please prefer --index-url over --extra-index-url, for security reasons.
Because pip does not lock dependencies to specific repositories, and because
pip provides no protection from package spoofing, we recommend using Keygen
as the sole package index. All non-Keygen packages will be securely
redirected to PyPI for fulfillment (also known as a "pass through"
PyPI repository).

This prevents pip from installing a package with the same name from PyPI
instead of Keygen, preventing a supply chain attack vector.

Alternatively, you can add the --index-url flag to your requirements.txt.

Alternatively, you can configure the engine globally via pypi.conf. This will
make pip install all packages through Keygen. Keygen is a pass-through
PyPI repository, meaning we will redirect all non-Keygen packages to PyPI.

Please see earlier security notice on --index-url vs --extra-index-url.

Alternatively, you can configure the engine globally via .pypirc.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support uploading Python packages via twine.
To upload a new version of a package, you can run python setup.py bdist_wheel sdist
and then use the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release,
then upload your whl and other distribution artifacts.

Keygen does not support Squirrel.Mac or Squirrel.Windows yet, but we have an official integration
with electron-builder that we recommend
instead. It is easier to integrate with across platforms, and more secure.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

The version constraint for the upgrade. For example, constraint=1.0 will constrain all upgrades to version 1.x, while constraint=1.0.0 will constrain to version 1.0.x. This is useful if a given license is only entitled to a specific version range. Major version is required.

You can also use constraints to constrain to a specific prerelease tag, such as constraint=1-beta, or to a specific build tag like constraint=1%2Bfoo (note the URL-encoded + symbol).

The release channel. One of: stable, rc, beta, alpha or dev. The rc channel will include stable releases. The beta channel will include rc and stable. Alpha will include beta, rc, and stable. Dev will only include releases on the dev channel (you can think of it as 'nightly' or 'edge', i.e. following a master branch).

A 200 OK response will be returned along with the update object.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

You can use Keygen with Tauri's native updater
to implement auto-updates for your Tauri app. Releases can be drafted
and artifacts uploaded via the CLI or UI.

Please note that signatures MUST be explicitly set on uploaded artifacts.
We do not automatically read accompanying .sig artifacts.

Using the CLI, this would look something like this:

The raw engine can be to create dynamic artifact download links that point to raw binaries, installers, etc.
These artifact download links are scoped to a product, package, and release. When the release does not have
a package, the package may be omitted.

You may also use the raw.pkg.keygen.sh subdomain, e.g. https://raw.pkg.keygen.sh/<account>/<product>[/@<package>]/<release>/<artifact>.

An authentication token with privileges to read the artifacts: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 303 See Other redirect will be returned, pointing to the artifact's canonical URL.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

# Electron engine

Source: https://keygen.sh/docs/api/engines/#engines-electron

Engines are automatically populated by the current packages and their
releases. The below endpoints are read-only. To activate an engine,
create a package implementing the desired engine e.g. pypi, npm,
rubygems, etc.

An authentication token with privileges to read the release engine: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated engines.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with an engine object.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

An authentication token with privileges to read the engines: either an admin, the product the releases belong to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated engines.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with a list of engine objects.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Keygen implements the OCI distribution specification for container registries. The OCI specification is compatible with tools like Docker, Helm, and Skopeo.
For more information on the OCI specification, see opencontainers/distribution-spec. In addition,
we attempt to maintain compatibility with the Docker distribution specification, which can be found at distribution/distribution.
Keygen's OCI engine is an OCI-compliantpull-only registry.

You may also use the oci.pkg.keygen.sh subdomain, e.g. https://oci.pkg.keygen.sh/<account>.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

Keygen implements PyPI's simple repository format for pip packages. Artifact metadata will be visible as data-* attributes, e.g. requiresPython will become data-requires-python.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with an HTML document containing
links to the package artifacts, in accordance with PEP 503.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the pypi engine using pip. Only
packages that implement the pypi engine will be available for
install. Packages for other engines, or packages without an
engine, will not be available.

In addition, only packages which are available to the current requestor
will be included, e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN
packages will be included.

Please prefer --index-url over --extra-index-url, for security reasons.
Because pip does not lock dependencies to specific repositories, and because
pip provides no protection from package spoofing, we recommend using Keygen
as the sole package index. All non-Keygen packages will be securely
redirected to PyPI for fulfillment (also known as a "pass through"
PyPI repository).

This prevents pip from installing a package with the same name from PyPI
instead of Keygen, preventing a supply chain attack vector.

Alternatively, you can add the --index-url flag to your requirements.txt.

Alternatively, you can configure the engine globally via pypi.conf. This will
make pip install all packages through Keygen. Keygen is a pass-through
PyPI repository, meaning we will redirect all non-Keygen packages to PyPI.

Please see earlier security notice on --index-url vs --extra-index-url.

Alternatively, you can configure the engine globally via .pypirc.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support uploading Python packages via twine.
To upload a new version of a package, you can run python setup.py bdist_wheel sdist
and then use the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release,
then upload your whl and other distribution artifacts.

Keygen does not support Squirrel.Mac or Squirrel.Windows yet, but we have an official integration
with electron-builder that we recommend
instead. It is easier to integrate with across platforms, and more secure.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

The version constraint for the upgrade. For example, constraint=1.0 will constrain all upgrades to version 1.x, while constraint=1.0.0 will constrain to version 1.0.x. This is useful if a given license is only entitled to a specific version range. Major version is required.

You can also use constraints to constrain to a specific prerelease tag, such as constraint=1-beta, or to a specific build tag like constraint=1%2Bfoo (note the URL-encoded + symbol).

The release channel. One of: stable, rc, beta, alpha or dev. The rc channel will include stable releases. The beta channel will include rc and stable. Alpha will include beta, rc, and stable. Dev will only include releases on the dev channel (you can think of it as 'nightly' or 'edge', i.e. following a master branch).

A 200 OK response will be returned along with the update object.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

You can use Keygen with Tauri's native updater
to implement auto-updates for your Tauri app. Releases can be drafted
and artifacts uploaded via the CLI or UI.

Please note that signatures MUST be explicitly set on uploaded artifacts.
We do not automatically read accompanying .sig artifacts.

If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

Engines are automatically populated by the current packages and their

Keygen implements the OCI distribution specification for container registries. The OCI specification is compatible with tools like Docker, Helm, and Skopeo.
For more information on the OCI specification, see opencontainers/distribution-spec. In addition,
we attempt to maintain compatibility with the Docker distribution specification, which can be found at distribution/distribution.
Keygen's OCI engine is an OCI-compliantpull-only registry.

You may also use the oci.pkg.keygen.sh subdomain, e.g. https://oci.pkg.keygen.sh/<account>.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Pull an image that implements the OCI engine using docker. Only packages that
implement the oci engine will be available for pull. Packages for other
engines, or packages without an engine, will not be available. In addition,
only packages which are available to the current requestor will be included,
e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN packages will be included.

Due to an upstream issue in the default
Docker Engine graphdriver storage engine (overlay2) i.r.t. how it handles authentication
in multi-tenant registries, you must use the containerd storage engine instead.
The default graphdriver engine does not respect registries that serve both unauthenticated
and authenticated requests, and is incompatible with Keygen's access control policies.
Instructions on enabling the containerd engine in Docker can be found here.
Docker Desktop has now transitioned
to containerd by default for new installs, and we expect the rest of the ecosystem
to follow.

For authentication, you have a couple options:

You can authenticate with a license key via docker login using --username license
and setting --password or --password-stdin to the license key value. The policy
must have an authentication strategy
of LICENSE or MIXED.

You can authenticate with an API token via --username token and setting
--password-stdin or --password to the token value. When using a license token,
the policy must have an authentication strategy
of TOKEN or MIXED.

Whether to use license keys vs tokens is a personal preference.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing images via docker push, and we
do not support other mutations such as deleting images or tags. Keygen's OCI
engine is a pull-only registry.

To upload a new version of an image, you can run docker build to build an OCI
image layout, and then use the Keygen CLI, the API, or the UI
to draft a new package release, then upload your image tar tarball.

The OCI engine ONLY supports images following the OCI image layout spec.
Uploading an image tarball that does not use an OCI image layout will fail
to be processed.

Similarly to Docker, you can use Oras to pull and inspect images. As with Docker,
please note that we DO NOT support pushing or deleting images or tags.
Rather, this can be performed via the Keygen CLI, UI, or API.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with the package metadata in JSON format.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Install a package that implements the npm engine using npm. Only packages that
implement the npm engine will be available for install. Packages for other
engines, or packages without an engine, will not be available. In addition,
only packages which are available to the current requestor will be included,
e.g. if you don't authenticate then only OPEN packages will be included.

For most use-cases, you'll be most successful using scoped packages, since it's
a lot easier to instruct npm to install all packages under @your-scope from a
private registry vs an unscoped package. In addition, we always recommend obtaining
the same scope on npm's public registry as well — otherwise a similarly named
package on the public npm registry may be installed instead of your package.

When installing packages via package.json, the easiest way to instruct npm to install
from your private registry is to use a package scope configured to point to a particular
registry — otherwise a similarly named package on the public npm registry may be
installed instead of your package.

You can instruct npm to install packages under a particular scope from a private
registry using an .npmrc file, or by configuring the registry via npm config.

Whether or not to use .npmrc vs npm config is a personal preference.

For authentication, you have a couple options:

You can set a license key using the :username and :_password parameters,
where :username is license and :_password is a base64-encoded license
key (note the value for :_password MUST be base64-encoded).

You can set an API token via the :_authToken= parameter.

Whether to use license keys vs tokens is a personal preference.

Notes on publishing

Please note that we DO NOT support pushing npm packages via npm push.
To upload a new version of a package, you can run npm pack and then use
the CLI or the UI to draft a new package release, then
upload your tgz tarball artifact.

An authentication token with privileges to read the releases: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If there are products with an OPEN distribution strategy, no authentication is required to read their associated releases.

An authentication token with privileges to read the package: either an admin, the product it belongs to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If the product's distribution strategy is OPEN, no authentication is required.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with a package object.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with the updated license object.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Permanently deletes a package. It cannot be undone. This action also immediately
deletes any releases and artifacts that the package is associated with.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.

Returns a list of packages. The packages are returned sorted by creation date,
with the most recent published packages appearing first. Resources are automatically
scoped to the authenticated bearer e.g. when authenticated as a license or user, only
packages accessible by the requestor will be listed.

An authentication token with privileges to read the packages: either an admin, the product the packages belong to, an entitled license (via license key or a license token), or a user with an entitled license. If the product's distribution strategy is OPEN, no authentication is required.

A 200 OK response will be returned along with a list of package objects.

Upon error, an errors object will be returned along with an
HTTP status code indicating the type of error. When an error occurs, the
data property will not be included.
